error_note: Hypoglycemia is an unquantified, nonspecific feature of complex I deficiency (207 diseases carry it), and a low glucose 6 h after a glucose load is reactive hypoglycemia rather than the fasting/metabolic hypoglycemia annotated.
An amphiphysin antibody titer is not total CSF protein; a low or absent titer is the normal result and has no bearing on NGLY1 deficiency.

LH 2 h after a triple-bolus (GnRH-containing) stimulation is a stimulated value; a high result needs its own criteria and is not the basal LH elevation annotated for premature ovarian failure, although an exaggerated response does occur in it.
Lactic acidosis is a real feature of complex I deficiency, but the code is an unspecified (XXX) challenge timepoint so 'high' is undefined, and elevated lactate is shared by 244 diseases.
Elevated lactate is a real feature of ECHS1 deficiency, but the code is an unspecified (XXX) challenge timepoint so 'high' is undefined, and elevated lactate is shared by 244 diseases.
LDL 3 is one LDL subfraction reported as a molar concentration, not LDL cholesterol; a low subfraction does not by itself show decreased LDL-C, though it would usually be low in this disease.

Urinary PBG is characteristically not increased in ALAD porphyria (ALA is the raised marker); this pertinent negative is coded as a biomarker with expected result 'other', which does not convey the intended meaning.

A negative IgE to one plant (arrowroot) says almost nothing about the whole class of anti-plant-product IgE; the term is far broader than the test, and a plant-based food allergen term fits better. The code is also deprecated.
Elevated VLDL cholesterol is not a recognised feature of Johanson-Blizzard syndrome; the annotation has no frequency and looks like an incidental case-report finding.

'Leukocytes other' counts unclassified/other cells on a manual differential, not the total leukocyte count; in addition leukocytosis is annotated as very rare in amoebiasis and is shared by 125 diseases.

AChR antibody positivity is explicitly excluded (0%) in congenital myasthenic syndrome 2C; absence of these antibodies is what separates it from autoimmune myasthenia, yet a positive association was emitted.

The immunoglobulin abnormality is annotated as excluded (0%) in this disease, and independently a low cockatiel-feather IgE fraction is a normal result that says nothing about total immunoglobulin concentrations.

A low CSF leukocyte count is the normal state; the CSF abnormality of superficial siderosis is xanthochromia/red cells/raised iron or protein, which the near-root 'Abnormal CSF morphology' bridge hides.

A low fruit-allergen-mix IgE is a normal result and is not a measure of circulating immunoglobulin concentration; the immunoglobulin abnormalities of lysinuric protein intolerance concern total IgG/subclasses.

A low glucose value is numerically hypoglycemia, but the code is an unspecified (XXX) challenge timepoint, so 'low' has no defined reference and may be the intended effect of the challenge (e.g. insulin).
The test measures IgG4, not IgE, and gelatin is an animal-derived product, not a plant-based food; a normal gelatin IgG4 cannot rule out raised plant-food IgE.

ACTH is expected to rise after CRH; a high post-CRH value means an exaggerated response (as in Cushing disease) by test-specific criteria and is not the basal 'Increased circulating ACTH level' phenotype.

A single-frequency, single-ear threshold stands in for pure-tone audiometry as a whole, and audiometry documents the hearing-loss component rather than diagnosing Usher syndrome type 4, which needs retinal and molecular confirmation.

One frequency in one ear stands in for a full audiologic assessment; it characterises sensorineural loss but cannot by itself diagnose aminoglycoside-induced deafness, which rests on exposure history and MT-RNR1 testing.

60 mg/dL is the ATP III protective-risk cut-off and lies within the normal range (near the mean for women); using it as the threshold for the abnormality phenotype 'Elevated HDL-C' (hyperalphalipoproteinemia) over-calls it, and the context note for the second band is internally inconsistent (mentions a LOW outcome).
Child-Pugh grades severity in a patient already known to have cirrhosis; the score (minimum 5 in anyone) does not itself demonstrate cirrhosis.
NYHA class is a functional grading whose limiting symptom may be fatigue, palpitation or angina as well as dyspnea; class IV usually implies dyspnea at rest but does not specifically establish it.

The statement that an untimed vancomycin level is uninformative about acute kidney injury is true but is a null assertion rather than an association; a drug level is at most a nephrotoxicity risk marker and AKI is not what the test measures. No code covers a vacuous 'uninformative' claim.

The at-target band (<6.0 mg/dL on urate-lowering therapy) describes treated gout patients, whose hyperuricemia is suppressed rather than excluded, and it overlaps the 5.7-6.0 range that the female band counts as hyperuricemic.

A reactive treponemal immunoassay stays positive for life after treated infection and is a screening result needing a nontreponemal test; it indicates past or present exposure rather than current syphilis, as the curator text itself concedes.

A single normal glucose (fasting state not even specified by the code) cannot rule out the broad class 'Abnormal glucose homeostasis', which includes diabetes diagnosed by HbA1c/OGTT, impaired glucose tolerance and episodic hypoglycemia.
An eGFR of 15-29 gives GFR category G4, but stage 4 chronic kidney disease additionally requires persistence for more than 3 months; a single value cannot separate it from acute kidney injury.
